documents.title: Yeshiva University Undergraduate AI Policy
documents.summary: Undergraduate AI policy of the Provost's Office. It sets a five-level framework (UG 0 to UG 4), defaults every assignment to no AI, requires written disclosure above UG 0, and sets integrity, privacy, faculty-use, assessment and governance rules.
documents.stance_why: The policy offers named tiers, so stance is delegates by the CODEBOOK rule. Its own words: "The colleges neither prohibit AI outright nor require it. Faculty decide how AI fits the learning goals of their courses", with "If no level is stated anywhere, the level is UG 0" as the fallback. The default is restrictive; unit-level codes carry that (P01, P06).

notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. Coder A notes: Coded independently (Coder A). The UG policy PDF is dated August 2026 and still has "[DATE]" for its effective date. Doc 2 is an IT policy for faculty and staff (internal document); its PDF text is one word per line and the properties table mislabels the title as an Incident Response Plan. Doc 3 is a wider resources page; Proctorio, electronic-exam logistics and time-management links were skipped as not about AI. Doc 3 template sentences that repeat across templates (e.g. the generative-AI ban) were coded once. Course layer deferred in the collect file. No new types proposed; UNCOVERED units: ask-safe-harbor and instructor duty to answer permission questions. [undergrad-ai-policy B#116] Appendix A heading only ('Appendix A: Sample Syllabus Statements'); a heading, not a policy statement. [undergrad-ai-policy B#118] Appendix B instruction repeats Section 7.1 ('The assignment-level policy belongs on the assignment itself'), already coded; dropped as a repeat. [academic-integrity-resources B#11] Template heading 'AI Use Policy (Assistive Only).' only; the template's rules are coded from its own sentences.
